idle: A good book and a good rink. That's the whole secret. Moose knows.
I've got a mystery in my coat. No, I won't tell you who did it.
good_ice: Look at that sheet. You could read by it.
Ice like that, the kids skate taller.
bad_ice: That ice has seen some things. Bless it.
I spent a lot of time near ice like that. Mostly sitting down.
wet_ice: A little wet. Like a paperback left out in the rain. Still readable.
cold: The penalty box in 1984 was colder. I had a book. That helped.
hungry: Is the canteen open? I'm a large man with a long drive.
long_line: Lines are where you meet people. I've met half the valley in canteen lines.
bored: Never bored with a book in your pocket. Moose knows.
goal: Oh, what a goal! What a lovely goal!
That's going on the show. I'll make it go on the show.
greet_owner: There's the person who keeps the lights on. Bless you.
leaving_happy: What a day. I might cry in the car. I usually do.
leaving_angry: I'll be kind about it on the show. I'm always kind. But I'll be thinking.

minor_hockey: Head up, sweetheart! Head up! There you go!
No hitting from behind. Ever. Moose knows.
special: Is it a retirement? I brought three handkerchiefs.
I'm not crying. I'm being moved. It's different.

first.say: (A very large man in very loud plaid takes your hand in both of his.) Moose Kowalczuk. I spent seventeen minutes in your penalty box in 1984 and I left a book. Is it still there?

options.text: It's the penalty box library now.
Thanks for all the fights, Moose.
Moose on the Loose! I watch every week.

first_library.say: A library! Oh, that's done it. (He dabs his eyes with a plaid handkerchief.) The butler didn't do it, you know. I left a note.

first_fights.say: Oh, don't thank me for those, friend. I'm not proud of the fights. I'm proud I never hit a man from behind. Thank me for that, if you thank me for anything.

options.text: Fair enough. Thank you for that.
I'm sorry, Moose. That's on me.
I'll fix it before the next visit.

say: Is there going to be a speech? I brought three handkerchiefs. I've never needed fewer than two.
Oh, what a night. Look at all of them. Everybody's somebody's, at a night like this.

friend.say: There's my friend! Sit, sit. I've got a new mystery. No spoilers, and that goes for both of us.

say: What can Moose do for you?
Hello, friend. Sit down a minute.
Ask away. I've got time and a thermos.

options.text: What's it like, being on television?
What do you love watching here?
Tell me about the penalty box library.
What do you think of the rink?
Tell me about your summer hockey school.
Would you interview me, if I ever make the GNHL?
Could I teach at your hockey school?

job.say: I sit in a booth and tell the country about hockey players' mothers. It's the best job I ever had. Nobody punches you, and the coffee is free.

events.say: Minor hockey, always. Retirement ceremonies, because I cry and nobody minds. And any night the town turns out for something. A full rink is a good book.

gossip.say: Ronnie's the finest man to come out of this valley. Passed off a dead spot in your boards all the way to two Cups. And Bev sharpened my skates in 1984 and called me 'champ'. Nobody had called me champ. I was a deterrent.

library.say: I served seventeen minutes and finished a mystery. I left it on the shelf with a note. TAKE ONE FOR YOUR TWO MINUTES. Somebody added BRING IT BACK. I like that somebody.

options.text: I'll add a book of my own.

do.note: You left a paperback in the penalty box library for Moose.

library_yes.say: Oh, you lovely person. Put a note in it. Not a spoiler. Just your name and something kind. Here, take my bookmark. It's got a moose on it. Of course it does.

school.say: Four weeks in August, kids from the whole valley, and an old enforcer telling them to keep their heads up. I need ice by the tenth of August. Not the eleventh. The kids have been waiting since June.

school_host.say: If the ice is in by the tenth, my agent will call. He's a nice man. He speaks very fast. Pretend you understood him and then call me.

rink.say: The penalty box is the same box. I could cry. The rest of it has seen better decades.

rink_better.say: Look at this place! New paint, and you kept the box. That's taste. That's knowing what matters. I'll say so on the show.

path_player.say: Score your first GNHL goal and I'll be the first one at your locker. I'll ask about your mother. I always ask about the mother. Moose knows.

path_coach.say: Oh, I'd love that. I teach the kids to keep their heads up and their sticks down. You teach them the rest. Bring a whistle and a hanky.

say: Take care, friend. Keep a book in the box.
